title: Op Decklets: surgical kits for incident remediation and safe admin flows
creator: Jordan Lee
description:
Problem: oncall responders need small, low-blast-radius admin actions to fix common production issues (clear a stale cache key, restart a single replica, rotate a model alias) without running a full runbook or escalating to SRE. Current runbooks are long, hard to parse under pressure, and often require CLI access or wide-scoped credentials.

Goal: deliver a set of composable 'Op Decklets' — parameterized, pre-authorized, audited admin utilities that run as first-class tasks in the Console and via opsctl. Decklets must be idempotent, include dry-run and verification steps, surface cost/latency impact, and emit structured telemetry and audit events. They should support canary scope, automatic rollback on post-check failure, and easy composition into larger runbooks.

Out-of-scope: full replacement of existing runbook DSL; heavy-weight orchestration for multi-step incident remediations (we will compose decklets into those runbooks instead).
acceptance_criteria: Decklet manifest format defined and validated (name, inputs schema, permission scope, dry_run flag, verification queries, rollback action)
Console can render a decklet form with typed inputs and execute in 'dry run' and 'execute' modes
Decklet execution path runs with least-privilege token, produces an audit event containing correlation_id, inputs (redacted), and outcome
Each decklet has a required post-check; if post-check fails, system triggers configured rollback action and surfaces trace in Console
Telemetry events are emitted for start/finish/dry-run/rollback with latency and token usage metrics
Opsctl CLI supports decklet discovery and safe local dry-run via a sandbox mode
End-to-end tests for three canonical decklets (cache-clear, single-replica-restart, model-alias-rotate) pass in CI and staging
tasks: Define decklet manifest schema and validator (JSON Schema) - runtime + console teams
Implement runtime enforcement hook that exchanges decklet-scope tokens and executes under least privilege
Console UI: form renderer, dry-run toggle, confirmation modal with blast-radius estimate
Audit + telemetry: structured events (decklet.exec.start, decklet.exec.end, decklet.exec.rollback) and correlation header implementation
Opsctl integration: discovery command, dry-run sandbox that executes verification queries without state mutation
Acceptance tests: unit tests for validator, integration tests for runtime hook, e2e for three canonical decklets
Docs and playbook gallery: authoring guide, example decklets, security guidance for least-privilege scoping
progress_updates: 2025-02-03: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, Console, and Security. Agreed on 'decklet' semantics: single atomic mutation with idempotent verification and optional rollback.

2025-02-10: Schema sketch reviewed — JSON Schema draft 0.1 includes 'inputs', 'permission_scope', 'verification', 'rollback', and 'blast_radius_hint'. Security requested explicit redact rules for secrets in telemetry.

2025-02-18: Samir opened proto PR implementing manifest validator and runtime hook stub (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4216). Initial unit tests added. CI failing on RBAC token exchange due to dependency ENG-271443 (limited-scope token service).

2025-02-25: Console team shipped form renderer prototype behind feature flag (console-ff/decklets). UX feedback: require clearer rollback descriptions and better error formatting for verification failures.

2025-03-01: Security ran threat model and requested A) explicit auditing of who invoked decklet, B) retention policy for decklet logs, C) guardrail preventing decklets from granting new privileges. Added to checklist.

2025-03-04: Integration test for 'cache-clear' decklet green in staging using the sandbox token; discovered flaky verification query under high load — added to risk notes and created follow-up ENG-246825 to harden verification queries.
decisions: Use JSON Schema for manifest validation to allow cross-language tooling and editor integration
Decklets will always run via an intermediate 'decklet-executor' service that exchanges customer tokens for scoped ephemeral tokens — no direct execution from Console frontend
Default embargo: decklets marked 'sensitive' require approval from the security rotation group before being publishable to the org-wide gallery
Telemetry will redact inputs by default; allowed input whitelist for non-sensitive fields will be configurable per-decklet
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: mistaken authoring could create high-blast operations. Mitigation: implement manifest Lint with blast_radius warnings, and require a manual two-step approval for high-blast decklets.
Risk: rollback may fail if external system in different state. Mitigation: require idempotent compensating actions and surface rollback status clearly; ensure ops-oncall gets automatic notification
Risk: telemetry could leak PII. Mitigation: security-required redact rules and retention policy; decklet lint will fail on non-redacted patterns
review_feedback: PM (Riley Morgan): prefer visible 'blast-radius' meter in the Console; add estimated token cost per decklet execution
Design (Priya Anand): suggested inline examples for common inputs and microcopy to explain dry-run vs execute semantics
Security (Evan Ortiz): require explicit 'can_run_as' scope in manifest and deny-list for 'super-admin' actions
Runtime (Ling Chen): asked for a small compatibility shim so old runbook steps can be wrapped as decklets with a migration tool
